clue.text: Poetic rhythm in simple time

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for time sits inside the word for simple

parts.note: mere means simple or nothing more than

explanation.surface: A note on verse whose beat is as plain as a musical bar in simple time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Simple time' looks like a musical term belonging with the rhythm, but 'simple' is MERE and 'time' is T, put inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Metre is the regular pattern of stressed syllables that gives verse its beat.

clue.text: A grim era dispelled with liberty under Union charter

indicators.note: in a down clue under means the liberty word comes below the anagram
dispelled suggests the letters are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: licence means freedom or liberty

explanation.surface: A dark period ended by a liberating charter for a union of states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispelled' rearranges A GRIM ERA. 'Union' looks political but means wedlock.
explanation.definitionFit: The document is the official permit that allows a wedding, a union of two people.

clue.text: It's bound, they say, to produce confidence

indicators.note: they say signals that the word for bound is heard spoken, not written

parts.note: trussed means tied up, bound

explanation.surface: A claim that something is certain to build confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'certain to', but it means tied up.
explanation.definitionFit: Trust is firm belief in someone's reliability.

clue.text: Finish mice off, prevalent in the area

parts.note: end means finish

indicators.note: off in the sense of gone bad or wrong, so the letters of mice are disordered

explanation.surface: Getting rid of mice that are rife in the district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' rearranges MICE to EMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease that is endemic is regularly found in a particular region.

clue.text: Not active when one's in Opposition

definitions.note: opposition here is the act of opposing, matched by the participle meaning fighting against

indicators.note: the clue's in places one's inside the words for not active

parts.note: resting means idle, not active
one's read as one is, giving I plus S, i.e. IS

explanation.surface: A politician idling on the Opposition benches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' is read as 'one is'. The capital on 'Opposition' suggests Parliament's opposing party, but it just means standing against.
explanation.definitionFit: Those in opposition are fighting against something, which is what resisting means.

clue.text: Lover coming to premature end in Italian city

indicators.note: a premature end means the final letter of the lover word is cut off

parts.note: Romeo, Shakespeare's young lover, gives a name for any lover

explanation.surface: A lover who dies young in Italy, as Shakespeare's hero did in Verona.
explanation.definitionFit: Rome is the capital of Italy.

clue.text: Such people, 'if foolish, burn with heat in seconds

definitions.text: Such people, 'if foolish, burn with heat in seconds

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters between two seconds

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second, so seconds gives two of them

indicators.note: foolish suggests the letters behave madly and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that careless people lying in the sun will get burnt very quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foolish' signals the anagram of the two words inside two Ss (seconds). Read whole, the clue also describes the answer's careless habit.
explanation.definitionFit: People lying out in strong sun who are careless will quickly get sunburnt.

clue.text: Setting up specialised terminology is required for communications system

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting up means the letters are raised so they read upwards

parts.note: slang is informal vocabulary used by a particular group

explanation.surface: Developing jargon is needed to run a communications network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setting up' turns SLANG and IS together, so SLANGIS read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Signals are the means by which messages are sent, as in an army's signals corps.

clue.text: Detachment I also ordered into riot

indicators.note: ordered says the letters of also are put into a new order
riot suggests disorder, so the letters of into run wild

explanation.surface: Someone sent off alone after being ordered into a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams with their own indicators, 'ordered' and 'riot', follow the I; 'riot' looks like a noun in the surface but is the second signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Detachment is being cut off or kept apart from others.

clue.text: Plucky resistance secures English striker's comprehensive victory

parts.note: game means plucky, willing to have a go

indicators.note: secures means the resistance word holds the English letter

parts.note: a stand is a stout resistance, as in make a stand
a match is struck to make fire

explanation.surface: A brave defence holds out against an English footballer in a decisive win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' looks like a footballer but is a match.
explanation.definitionFit: The tennis phrase announces a player has won outright, so it means total victory.

clue.text: They regularly deliver ammunition to soldiers

parts.note: rounds are cartridges or shells, units of ammunition
men is the usual crossword word for soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A supply chain bringing ammunition to troops in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: Roundsmen are tradesmen such as milkmen who deliver along a fixed route; the surface makes the deliveries military.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundsman makes the same delivery round every day, so their visits are regular.

clue.text: Train with compass after midnight

indicators.note: after says the compass word follows the midnight letter

parts.note: the middle of the word night is its letter G
compass in the sense of scope or space, i.e. room

explanation.surface: A navigator training with a compass in the small hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midnight' is read as the middle of 'night', its third letter G. 'Compass' means range or scope, not the direction-finder.
explanation.definitionFit: To groom someone is to prepare or coach them for a role.

clue.text: Meeting a deadline, eventually

definitions.meaning: arriving before the time limit runs out
sooner or later, given long enough

explanation.surface: Someone who gets there in the end, just about meeting the deadline.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both punctual enough and, given time, in the end.

clue.text: Vehicles used by travel companies in the desert

definitions.meaning: trailers towed behind cars for holidays
groups of merchants crossing desert lands together, often with camels

explanation.surface: Holiday firms using motor homes for desert tours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used by' is just a link between the two senses; 'companies' means groups travelling together, not firms.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both towed holiday homes and convoys of camel traders.

clue.text: One travelling by air to make a blood transfusion

definitions.text: One travelling by air to make a blood transfusion

parts.words: One travelling by air to make a blood transfusion
parts.note: sounds like a flying medic or blood courier, but describes a winged creature that feeds on blood

explanation.surface: A medic flying in to give a patient blood.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'transfusion' is from the victim into the creature, which feeds on blood.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin American flying mammal lives on the blood of other animals.

clue.text: Attendance at failing show up unexpectedly

parts.note: gate is the number of spectators at a match
to crash is to fail, as a business or computer does

explanation.surface: Poor turnout at a flop of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: GATE is the British term for attendance at a sports event. 'Show' looks like a noun but belongs to the definition as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn up uninvited at a party is to arrive where you were not expected.

clue.text: Is "Water Music" appropriate for such a performer?

definitions.text: Is "Water Music" appropriate for such a performer?

parts.words: Is "Water Music" appropriate for such a performer?
parts.note: Handel's suite suggests an orchestra, but water comes from a tap, so this dancer would suit it

explanation.surface: A question about whether Handel's suite suits a certain dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: Water Music is Handel's orchestral suite; the joke is that water comes from a tap.
explanation.definitionFit: This performer dances in metal-plated shoes that rap out rhythms.

clue.text: It's expedient to make a move

definitions.meaning: a dodge or stratagem used to get by

explanation.surface: Advice that moving on would be the convenient choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expedient' is a noun here, a contrivance, not the adjective meaning convenient.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a trick or makeshift and to change position.

clue.text: Removes some branches, keeping copse finally within bounds

indicators.note: keeping says the branch-trimming word holds the next letter

parts.note: to lop is to cut branches off a tree

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word copse

explanation.surface: A tree surgeon pruning branches and keeping the copse tidy within its boundaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Within bounds' sounds like limits, but 'bounds' is the definition, a verb meaning leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To lope is to run with long, springing strides.

clue.text: Hide away in quarters on island

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the quarters sit above the island

parts.note: S and E are compass points, or quarters
Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: Someone hiding out in lodgings on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarters' looks like lodgings but means two compass points, S and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete something is to conceal it.

clue.text: Role taken by female performing in classical masterpiece

parts.note: a part is an actor's role
a hen is a female bird
on means performing, as an actor is on stage

explanation.surface: An actress taking a role in a classical play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classical masterpiece' suggests a play, but it is the Athens temple.
explanation.definitionFit: The temple to Athena on the Acropolis is the great masterwork of ancient Greek architecture.

clue.text: Locks in place with this security device

definitions.text: Locks in place with this security device

parts.words: Locks in place with this security device
parts.note: locks suggests doors, but they are locks of hair held by a pin

explanation.surface: A security gadget holding a lock shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' means hair, not door fastenings.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent wire pin holds hair in place.

clue.text: Opening lines in court

parts.note: an opening is an opportunity, a chance
RY is the abbreviation for railway, i.e. lines

explanation.surface: A barrister's opening remarks in the courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening lines' reads as the start of a speech; 'lines' is the railway (RY), a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Chancery was the Lord Chancellor's court and is now a division of the English High Court.

clue.text: Look in media tomorrow for microscopic organism

indicators.note: Look in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A suggestion to watch tomorrow's papers for a story about tiny life.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft definition included 'for', which is a link word, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: These single-celled algae with silica shells are far too small to see without a microscope.

clue.text: Unexpected development for Dickensian hero

definitions.meaning: a surprising turn in a story
Oliver, the orphan in Dickens's novel

explanation.surface: A plot surprise for one of Dickens's heroes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a surprise turn in a plot and the surname of Dickens's orphan Oliver.

clue.text: Responsibility for tax

definitions.meaning: a levy on goods, such as customs charges

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a moral obligation and a levy on imports.

clue.text: Appropriate place husband found, in pleasant surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings says the pleasant word is wrapped around the letter for husband

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: A husband settling into a comfortable spot in nice surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a role or position that suits someone exactly.

clue.text: Plan of athlete to replace leader in race

indicators.note: the athlete's word takes the place of the first letter of the race word

parts.note: a sprint is a short fast race
a Blue is a sportsperson who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University

explanation.surface: A coach's strategy for an athlete to overtake the front-runner.
explanation.walkthrough: A BLUE is an Oxford or Cambridge sportsperson. Swapping the S at the front of SPRINT for BLUE gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A blueprint is a detailed design or scheme drawn up in advance.

clue.text: Showing determination, in good time to secure comfortable home

indicators.note: secure in the sense of hold, so the early word encloses the home word

parts.note: early means ahead of time
a nest is a snug home

explanation.surface: Getting in early to buy a cosy house.
explanation.definitionFit: To act earnestly is to act seriously and with sincere resolve.

clue.text: Score of religious books housed in new church

indicators.note: housed in puts the religious books inside the new church letters

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of religious books

explanation.surface: Twenty sacred volumes kept in a newly built church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' looks like twenty, but it means a cut or nick.
explanation.definitionFit: To score a surface is to cut a mark in it, as a notch is cut.
